packageText: === MASTER SOURCE PACKAGE === TITLE: Abdominal Abscess SOURCE SYNTHESIS: RadPrimer canonical backbone with STATdx supplemental depth === CANONICAL HIERARCHY === All Categories > Basic > Gastrointestinal > Peritoneum, Mesentery, and Abdominal Wall > Abdominal Abscess Canonical deck path: Corebook::GI::Peritoneum, Mesentery, and Abdominal Wall::Abdominal Abscess Routing note: canonicalHierarchy is copied exactly from metadata.json; STATdx breadcrumbs were not used for deck routing. === SOURCE ATTRIBUTION RULES === - [Both] = supported by both RadPrimer and STATdx source packages. - [RadPrimer] = RadPrimer-only or RadPrimer-preferred canonical detail. - [STATdx] = supplemental STATdx detail, image example, or wording nuance. === IMAGE COVERAGE GATE === STATdx does not fully cover the RadPrimer image set. RadPrimer image 2 has exact STATdx duplicates; RadPrimer images 8 and 9 have near-duplicate/same-concept reinforcement; RadPrimer image 10 is not covered. - RadPrimer image 1: conceptualReplacement; related STATdx images: STATdx image 12, STATdx image 18. STATdx includes postoperative abscess examples, but no exact duplicate of this rounded gas-containing postoperative collection. - RadPrimer image 2: exactDuplicate; related STATdx images: STATdx image 11, STATdx image 17, STATdx image 12, STATdx image 18. STATdx images 11 and 17 are the same axial CT slice/content; STATdx images 12 and 18 are adjacent/same-patient reinforcement rather than duplicates. - RadPrimer image 3: conceptualReplacement; related STATdx images: STATdx image 5, STATdx image 6, STATdx image 10. STATdx has pelvic abscess examples, especially MR/CT pelvic cases, but not the same post-hysterectomy CT image. - RadPrimer image 4: conceptualReplacement; related STATdx images: STATdx image 2, STATdx image 26. STATdx includes drainage catheter follow-up examples, but not this transgluteal drainage image. - RadPrimer image 5: conceptualReplacement; related STATdx images: STATdx image 3, STATdx image 13, STATdx image 15, STATdx image 16. STATdx covers perforation-related abscess and gas-forming collections but does not exactly reproduce this free intraperitoneal gas image. - RadPrimer image 6: conceptualReplacement; related STATdx images: STATdx image 3, STATdx image 13, STATdx image 15, STATdx image 16. STATdx provides diverticulitis/perforation abscess cases, but this same-patient sigmoid diverticulosis/abscess slice is not duplicated. - RadPrimer image 7: conceptualReplacement; related STATdx images: STATdx image 8, STATdx image 13. STATdx includes gas-forming/retroperitoneal or lesser sac infected collections, but not the ERCP duodenal perforation case. - RadPrimer image 8: nearDuplicate; related STATdx images: STATdx image 4. STATdx image 4 is the same GIST mimic teaching concept and likely same case family, but it is a different CT slice/image, so both remain primary. - RadPrimer image 9: nearDuplicate; related STATdx images: STATdx image 9, STATdx image 10. STATdx images 9 and 10 provide tuboovarian abscess ultrasound/CT reinforcement; the ultrasound appearance is visually distinct and not an exact duplicate. - RadPrimer image 10: notCovered; related STATdx images: none. No STATdx staged image shows the same right psoas/Crohn-related MR abscess teaching point. === KEY FACTS === - [Both] Abdominal abscess is a localized abdominal collection of pus or infected fluid. - [Both] Best CT clue: low-density, loculated, encapsulated fluid collection with peripheral rim enhancement, with or without gas bubbles or an air-fluid level. - [Both] Internal gas without recent intervention is highly suspicious for infection, though gas can also reflect bowel communication. - [Both] Use the term abscess for a discrete, drainable collection; separate this from ill-defined inflammatory phlegmon or nondrainable fluid. - [Both] Adjacent fat stranding, edema, fascial thickening, and low-density parenchymal edema around intraparenchymal abscesses support infection. - [Both] Ultrasound shows a complex fluid collection with low-level echoes, membranes, septations, avascular center, and peripheral hyperemia. - [Both] Abscesses are common in postoperative, diabetic, and immunocompromised patients and may follow enteric perforation, bacteremia, or trauma. - [Both] Differentiating abscess from noninfected postoperative collection can require symptoms, labs, aspiration, or follow-up. === TERMINOLOGY === - [Both] Definition: localized abdominal collection of pus or infected fluid. === IMAGING === - [Both] General feature: loculated, encapsulated fluid collection with peripheral rim enhancement on contrast-enhanced CT. - [RadPrimer] Size is highly variable, often 2-15 cm, with microabscesses smaller than 2 cm. - [STATdx] Tiny microabscesses can be smaller than 1 cm, and small abscesses can be technically difficult to drain. - [Both] Location can be intraperitoneal, extraperitoneal, or intraparenchymal. - [Both] CT: simple fluid attenuation or mildly hyperdense content; surrounding inflammatory change is common. - [Both] CT: intraparenchymal abscesses in liver, kidney, spleen, and other organs often have surrounding low-density edema. - [RadPrimer] About half of abscesses contain internal gas; absence of gas does not exclude abscess. - [Both] MR: central low T1/high T2 fluid signal, peripheral rim enhancement on contrast-enhanced T1, and often restricted diffusion with low ADC. - [STATdx] Surrounding edema is especially conspicuous on fat-saturated sequences, particularly T2 fat-saturated imaging. - [Both] US: internal debris, septations, low-level echoes, variable through transmission, avascular center, peripheral hyperemia, and echogenic inflamed fat. - [Both] US gas clue: echogenic foci with ring-down artifact or dirty posterior acoustic shadowing. - [Both] Radiography may show a soft-tissue mass/density, loss of fat interface, ectopic gas or air-fluid levels, focal ileus, and subphrenic-related pleural effusion/atelectasis. - [Both] Abscess sinogram after drainage can assess residual cavity, catheter position, and fistulization to bowel, pancreas, or biliary tree. - [Both] Nuclear medicine options include labeled white blood cell imaging, gallium, and FDG PET, with PET sensitive but nonspecific. - [Both] Best imaging tool: contrast-enhanced CT. === DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS === - [Both] Postoperative lymphocele: lymph node dissection history; simple fluid along lymphatic drainage pathways near clips; no enhancing rim or gas. - [Both] Biloma: collection near biliary tree after biliary/hepatic surgery; usually simple unless infected. - [Both] Postoperative seroma: simple fluid, sometimes loculated or with recent postoperative gas; may be indistinguishable from abscess without clinical correlation. - [Both] Loculated ascites: minimal mass effect, no rim enhancement, no internal gas, often in cirrhosis or chronic systemic disease. - [Both] Pancreatic pseudocyst: pancreatitis history or stigmata; pseudocapsule generally develops over weeks. - [Both] Hematoma: attenuation varies with age; acute clot is often high attenuation and may weakly enhance peripherally during evolution. - [Both] Retained oxidized cellulose/Surgicel: postoperative gas collection with little fluid and no discrete drainable collection. - [Both] Cystic or necrotic neoplasm can mimic abscess, especially without fever, leukocytosis, or other infection history. === PATHOLOGY === - [Both] Etiologies include enteric perforation, postoperative infection, generalized bacteremia, and trauma. - [Both] Postoperative abscesses often occur in dependent intraperitoneal spaces such as cul-de-sac, Morison pouch, or subphrenic spaces. - [Both] Diabetic patients have increased risk for gas-forming abscesses; immunocompromised patients can develop fungal microabscesses. - [RadPrimer] Associated pathology includes pus, peripheral fibrocapillary capsule, and often polymicrobial enteric organisms. - [RadPrimer] Classification can be by organism, organ of origin, intra-/extraperitoneal location, or communication with bowel, biliary tree, or pancreatic duct. === CLINICAL ISSUES === - [Both] Presentation: fever, chills, abdominal pain, tachycardia, hypotension in sepsis, leukocytosis, positive blood cultures, or elevated ESR. - [Both] Older and immunocompromised patients may lack fever or elevated white blood cell count. - [Both] Prognosis is generally excellent with appropriate treatment but depends on abscess burden, immune status, and comorbidities. - [RadPrimer] Percutaneous abscess drainage has approximately 80% success with proper patient selection. - [Both] Ideal percutaneous drainage target: well-defined, encapsulated, fluid-filled abscess larger than 3 cm with safe catheter access. - [Both] CT or US guidance can support transcutaneous, transgluteal, transrectal, or transvaginal drainage approaches. - [Both] Complex multiseptated abscesses or abscesses with enteric fistula may require weeks to months; most drain in 10-14 days. - [Both] Catheter removal is considered when output is less than 10 cc per shift or the cavity resolves on imaging. - [Both] Patient-related drainage contraindications include coagulopathy, elevated INR, and platelets below 50,000/uL, using institution-specific thresholds. - [Both] Abscess-related drainage contraindications include phlegmon, no safe route, gas-forming infection such as emphysematous pancreatitis, echinococcal cyst, infected necrosis, multiseptated collection, or superinfected necrotic tumor. - [Both] Surgery may be needed for extensive intraperitoneal abscesses, debridement of necrotic infected tissue, or failed percutaneous drainage. - [Both] Small abscesses, usually smaller than 3 cm, may be treated with antibiotics alone; STATdx notes technical difficulty placing catheters in small abscesses. === DIAGNOSTIC CHECKLIST === - [Both] Correlate imaging with clinical signs, labs, aspiration, and postoperative timing when infected and noninfected collections overlap. - [Both] Do not require gas for diagnosis; an enhancing rim, mass effect, and inflammatory change can be highly suggestive in the right clinical context. - [Both] Avoid labeling nondrainable phlegmon as abscess when no discrete collection exists. === SELECTED PRIMARY IMAGE SET === - RadPrimer image 1: Axial CECT in an older postoperative patient demonstrates a rounded complex fluid collection with gas bubbles and an enhancing capsule , findings diagnostic for an abdominal abscess. Used for: primaryPattern, postoperativeAbscess, rimEnhancement, internalGas. - RadPrimer image 2: Axial CECT in an older postoperative patient demonstrates multiple loculated fluid collections with prominently enhancing capsules and mass effect on adjacent structures, representing abdominal abscesses. Note the air-fluid level within one of the abscesses. Used for: primaryPattern, multipleAbscesses, airFluidLevel, exactDuplicateAnchor. - RadPrimer image 3: Axial CECT shows a large pelvic abscess following a hysterectomy. Note the presence of a discrete enhancing rim and mass effect on adjacent loops of bowel and the bladder. Used for: pelvicAbscess, postoperativeAbscess, massEffect. - RadPrimer image 4: Axial CECT shows placement of a percutaneous drainage catheter using a transgluteal approach. The abscess has almost completely resolved following drainage. Used for: drainageFollowUp, transglutealApproach, procedureContext. - RadPrimer image 5: Axial CECT in a woman who presented with lower abdominal pain, fever, and tenderness shows extensive free intraperitoneal gas . Used for: samePatientCluster, entericPerforation, freeIntraperitonealGas. - RadPrimer image 6: Axial CECT in the same patient shows a loculated abscess immediately adjacent to a segment of sigmoid colon with extensive diverticulosis , which proved to be the source of the free air and abscesses. Used for: samePatientCluster, diverticularAbscess, sourceOfFreeAir. - RadPrimer image 7: Axial CECT after ERCP shows a large collection of gas and fluid dissecting through the retroperitoneal spaces, especially the anterior pararenal space and the interfascial plane . These findings were due to perforation of the duodenum at the papillotomy site. Used for: retroperitonealAbscess, duodenalPerforation, postERCPComplication. - RadPrimer image 8: Axial CECT demonstrates a large cystic mass with internal complexity. The mass was thought to represent an abscess and underwent unsuccessful drainage but was ultimately found to represent a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST). Used for: abscessMimic, cysticNeoplasm, GIST, recognitionReinforcement. - RadPrimer image 9: Ultrasound demonstrates a complex cystic mass with internal septations and multiple areas of higher echogenicity located in the right adnexa, representing a large tuboovarian abscess in this patient with pelvic inflammatory disease (PID). Used for: ultrasoundPattern, tuboovarianAbscess, internalSeptations. - RadPrimer image 10: Axial T1 C+ FS MR demonstrates a rim-enhancing abscess in the right psoas muscle. Note the phlegmonous change and enhancement around the margins of the abscess, partially attributable to inflammation from the patient's Crohn disease. Used for: mriPattern, psoasAbscess, CrohnDisease, phlegmon. - STATdx image 1: Axial CECT demonstrates a loculated fluid collection with prominent rim enhancement and surrounding soft tissue edema in the right lower quadrant, compatible with an abscess. The patient's appendix is partly visualized in the midst of this collection, compatible with perforated appendicitis. Used for: appendicealAbscess, alternateExample, recognitionReinforcement, samePatientCluster. - STATdx image 2: Axial CECT shows placement of a percutaneous drainage catheter into the abscess with a significant decrease in the size of the abscess following drainage. Used for: drainageFollowUp, appendicealAbscess, procedureContext, duplicateAnchor. - STATdx image 3: Axial CECT in a patient with pelvic pain and fever demonstrates a thick-walled enhancing fluid collection abutting the adjacent inflamed sigmoid colon , representing a peridiverticular abscess related to perforated diverticulitis. Used for: diverticulitisAbscess, alternateExample, recognitionReinforcement. - STATdx image 4: Axial CECT demonstrates a peripherally enhancing "fluid collection" abutting the left colon and small bowel. This was thought to be an abscess and even underwent unsuccessful drainage, but was ultimately found to represent a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST). Used for: abscessMimic, GIST, nearDuplicate, recognitionReinforcement. - STATdx image 5: Axial T1 C+ FS MR in a young female patient in septic shock demonstrates thick-walled, peripherally enhancing fluid collections in the pelvis, compatible with abscesses. Used for: mriPattern, pelvicAbscess, samePatientCluster. - STATdx image 6: Sagittal T2 MR in the same patient demonstrates the more anterior fluid collection is directly contiguous with the patient's C-section scar , compatible with uterine rupture as the cause for these abscesses. Note the presence of another large fluid collection more posteriorly between the uterus and rectum. Used for: mriPattern, uterineRupture, samePatientCluster, mechanism. - STATdx image 7: Axial CECT demonstrates a large, rim-enhancing abscess in the perineum secondary to traumatic Foley catheter placement and urethral perforation. Used for: perinealAbscess, traumaticFoley, unusualCause. - STATdx image 8: Axial CECT demonstrates a large, loculated fluid collection in the lesser sac with rim-enhancement and internal gas , representing an abscess with gas-forming infection. This infected collection was secondary to necrotizing pancreatitis. Used for: lesserSacAbscess, necrotizingPancreatitis, gasFormingInfection. - STATdx image 9: Transverse color Doppler US in a young female patient with pelvic pain and fever demonstrates a complex cystic adnexal mass without substantial color flow vascularity. Used for: ultrasoundPattern, tuboovarianAbscess, samePatientCluster, recognitionReinforcement. - STATdx image 10: Axial CECT in the same patient demonstrates a large fluid collection with rim enhancement and surrounding fat stranding (corresponding to the US finding), ultimately found to represent a tuboovarian abscess. Notice how the complexity in this collection is much more evident on US compared to CT. Used for: ctCorrelation, tuboovarianAbscess, samePatientCluster. - STATdx image 12: Axial CECT in the same patient shows ectopic gas bubbles within abscess in pelvis . Used for: samePatientCluster, postoperativeAbscess, adjacentSlice, internalGas. - STATdx image 13: Axial CECT of gas-forming retrocecal abscess from perforated diverticulum. Note ectopic gas collection from posterior to cecum , cecal thickening, and adjacent fat stranding . Used for: gasFormingAbscess, retrocecalAbscess, perforatedDiverticulum. - STATdx image 14: Transverse transabdominal US of a postoperative abscess found on a grayscale image is shown. Note the hypoechoic fluid collection with fluid-fluid level . Used for: ultrasoundPattern, postoperativeAbscess, fluidFluidLevel. - STATdx image 15: Axial CECT shows intramural abscess of the sigmoid from diverticulitis. Note the long segment of the markedly thickened sigmoid and an ill-defined adjacent fluid collection . Used for: samePatientCluster, intramuralSigmoidAbscess, diverticulitis. - STATdx image 16: Axial CECT in the same patient shows more discreet abscess collections on a lower plane of the section . Used for: samePatientCluster, intramuralSigmoidAbscess, adjacentSlice. - STATdx image 18: Axial CECT shows pyogenic postoperative abscess after bowel resection. Note multiple fluid collections with enhancing rims. Gas is noted in pelvic abscess but not in other collections. Used for: samePatientCluster, postoperativeAbscess, adjacentSlice, internalGas. - STATdx image 19: Axial CECT demonstrates a gas-forming pyogenic liver abscess in a diabetic patient. Note air-fluid level within the abscess cavity . Used for: liverAbscess, gasFormingInfection, diabetes, ctPattern. - STATdx image 20: Axial US shows a liver abscess demonstrating linear high-amplitude echoes with "dirty" distal acoustic shadowing representing gas . Used for: liverAbscess, ultrasoundPattern, dirtyShadowing, gas. - STATdx image 21: Axial CECT shows an amebic abscess. Note peripheral low-attenuation zone of edema surrounding the abscess. Used for: amebicAbscess, ctPattern, perilesionalEdema. - STATdx image 22: Sagittal US shows amebic abscess. Note low-level echoes within the hypoechoic mass, and the lack of distal acoustic enhancement. Used for: amebicAbscess, ultrasoundPattern, lowLevelEchoes. - STATdx image 23: Sagittal US shows fungal microabscesses due to systemic candidiasis. Note multiple target lesions . Used for: fungalMicroabscesses, immunocompromised, ultrasoundPattern. - STATdx image 24: Sagittal US of the spleen demonstrates an abscess with low-level echoes . Used for: splenicAbscess, ultrasoundPattern. - STATdx image 25: Axial CECT shows an encapsulated fluid collection with peripheral rim enhancement in the right lower quadrant. In the midst of the fluid collection is a tubular structure , representing a ruptured appendix. Used for: appendicealAbscess, nearDuplicate, samePatientCluster, recognitionReinforcement. - STATdx image 27: Axial CECT in a patient who underwent a cholecystectomy shows a collection of gas but very little fluid, in the cholecystectomy bed. Surgical clips are also seen. This represents oxidized cellulose (Surgicel), which was placed for hemostasis at surgery, and not an abscess. Used for: abscessMimic, Surgicel, postoperativeDifferential. === ARCHIVE-OPTIONAL DUPLICATE IMAGES === - STATdx image 11: archiveOptionalDuplicate. Visual inspection of staged image_evidence files shows the same axial CT slice/content as RadPrimer image 2, with only source encoding/crop differences. - STATdx image 17: archiveOptionalDuplicate. Visual inspection of staged image_evidence files shows the same axial CT slice/content as RadPrimer image 2, with only source encoding/crop differences. - STATdx image 26: archiveOptionalDuplicate. Visual inspection of staged image_evidence files shows the same appendiceal abscess drainage catheter CT image as STATdx image 2. === CASE CLUSTER NOTES === - RadPrimer images 5 and 6 are a same-patient free-air/diverticular abscess cluster and both remain selected. - STATdx image 12 and STATdx image 18 are adjacent/same-patient reinforcement images and remain selected even though their paired duplicate opening slices are archived. - STATdx image 2 preserves catheter follow-up context for the appendiceal abscess cluster after STATdx image 26 is archived as an exact duplicate. === GENERATOR INSTRUCTIONS === - Use this package as source material for later narrative/cards, but do not generate cards or lecture output during this synthesis step. - Use clean source-qualified labels in prose, such as RadPrimer image 5 and STATdx image 4. - Use registry IDs, source image IDs, hashes, and filenames for traceability and download routing.

sourceSelectionPlan.textBackbone: Use RadPrimer as the canonical hierarchy and article backbone; STATdx is used as supplemental depth where it adds modality-specific language, mechanisms, management nuance, differential mimics, or stronger image examples.
keepFromRadPrimer: Core imaging definition and CT/US/MR/radiographic/fluoroscopic/nuclear medicine structure.
Differential diagnosis list and PAD success/patient-selection details.
All RadPrimer images as selected primary images.
keepFromSTATdx: Small-abscess drainage nuance and fat-saturated MR edema emphasis.
Additional etiologic image examples: appendicitis, diverticulitis, uterine rupture, traumatic Foley, pancreatitis, liver/amebic/fungal/splenic abscesses, and Surgicel mimic.
All nonduplicate STATdx images as recognition reinforcement or supplemental cases.
downweightOrSkip: Do not repeat source-identical article prose twice.
Do not use STATdx breadcrumb/deck path for routing.

sourceSelectionPlan.imageCurationPolicy: Exact duplicates may be archived; near duplicates and conceptual replacements remain selected as recognition reinforcement unless visually identical or unusable.
sourceSelectionPlan.duplicateEvidencePolicy: ExactDuplicate decisions require visual evidence from image_evidence files, same stable source image ID, image hashes, or explicit manual/source confirmation. Caption-only or topic-only similarity must be marked uncertain/nearDuplicate and kept primary.
